new_findings.evidence: assess/decide return REJECT_STAGE_ORDER not only for an actual stage-order error but also when label_space != needs_review or auto_fraud violates policy.
new_findings.learner_failure: A reasonable learner can learn that auto_fraud=True is a pipeline-order defect instead of a prohibited decision-policy defect, producing the wrong remediation and audit trail.
new_findings.repair: Return separate tokens such as REJECT_LABEL_SPACE and REJECT_AUTO_FRAUD_POLICY; reserve REJECT_STAGE_ORDER for stages != CANON.

new_findings.evidence: decide(packet) checks score-only, uncertainty, evidence and graph_path, then returns CONTINUE, 4; it never requires case_id or score in the accepted path.
new_findings.learner_failure: A learner can pass an anonymous/unscored packet as ready for review and conclude that adding uncertainty compensates for missing identity/score.
new_findings.repair: Compose E3 with one canonical packet_ok validator that requires non-empty case_id, finite score in domain, non-empty source-backed evidence, graph path and uncertainty before counting explanation layers.

new_findings.evidence: The title/feedback require an appeal to reopen with another reviewer, but assess merely checks that second_reviewer is truthy; there is no original reviewer field or inequality test.
new_findings.learner_failure: A learner can set second_reviewer=ana when the original reviewer was also Ana and receive reopen, falsely believing an independent appeal occurred.
new_findings.repair: Include original_reviewer and require a distinct authorized second_reviewer; append an appeal audit event with actor, timestamp and reason.

new_findings.evidence: s.get('fp_rate', 0) > thr treats a missing per-slice fp_rate as zero, so a slice with no metric silently passes. It also does not validate rate/threshold domains or support counts.
new_findings.learner_failure: A learner can omit fp_rate for the most problematic subgroup and accidentally make the release look safer.
new_findings.repair: Require name, fp_rate and sample/support count for every slice; validate finite rates in [0,1] and a finite threshold in [0,1]; return REQUEST_SLICE_METRICS for any missing metric.

new_findings.evidence: The lesson calls the project cierre CP-N3-C, but the canonical CP-N3-C rubric requires baseline, reported calibration, cost-based threshold/human review, abstention, subgroup performance and model card. The starter uses a hand-built score, fixed thr=0.70, no baseline/calibration calculation and hard-coded subgroup/value metrics in Markdown cards.
new_findings.learner_failure: A learner can believe they completed CP-N3-C by packaging a toy score and static cards while never showing calibration, baseline or cost-threshold evidence.
new_findings.repair: Require versioned upstream baseline/calibration/threshold/subgroup artifacts with hashes/run IDs or compute them from a canonical fixture; gate ready_for_human_acceptance on those artifacts and their tests.

new_findings.evidence: S39 displays six percentage criteria totaling 100% plus rows whose weight values are literal bonus checklist, gate process, and gate privacy. The canonical CP-N3-C rubric instead uses four 0–3 criteria with weights .35/.20/.25/.20 and a gate rule >=2.4/3, no critical criterion <2, zero P0. SectionView renders every string under a column labeled Peso without reconciling the two contracts.
new_findings.learner_failure: A learner can optimize for the 25/20/20/15/10/10 table and still fail canonical calibration/abstention gates, or assume gate privacy is merely another weight row.
new_findings.repair: Use the canonical rubric as the S39 project rubric or explicitly label the local table checklist de preparación and link the canonical 0–3 rubric/hard gates. Render gate rows separately from numeric weights.

new_findings.evidence: The starter writes precision_at_k≈0.55, false_queue=0.08/0.11, override rates and median review time as literal text; says apelación con segundo revisor although no appeal workflow exists in the starter; and says rollback targets a versioned previous model although no model registry/rollback operation is implemented.
new_findings.learner_failure: A learner can learn to satisfy governance by writing plausible metrics/control statements into Markdown rather than attaching evidence that those controls ran.
new_findings.repair: Generate cards from validated run artifacts; include provenance for each metric/control, mark unavailable claims not_evaluated, and remove appeal/rollback claims until corresponding tests/events exist.

new_findings.evidence: Theory states that an override audit event needs actor, reason and timestamp. The I Do reduces evidence to audit: True; the You Do JSONL records run_id/case/path/action/score/override/human_only but no actor, reason, timestamp, model/threshold/policy version or appeal linkage.
new_findings.learner_failure: A learner can produce audit.jsonl that cannot answer who overrode what policy, why, or under which model/threshold version.
new_findings.repair: Add stable pseudonymous actor/reviewer ID, reason code, timestamp, original auto action, final action, model_id, threshold/policy version, appeal linkage and append-only integrity checks.

new_findings.evidence: BRIEF says the dataset contains case_id, features, label, subgrupo, timestamp, cost_fp and cost_fn. data/generate.py instead emits generic records with id, name, email, amount and status and no ML labels/cost/subgroup/timestamp fields.
new_findings.learner_failure: A learner following the canonical dataset path cannot implement cost-based thresholds, temporal/subgroup checks or labeled calibration because the required fields do not exist.
new_findings.repair: Replace the generic generator with deterministic CP-N3-C cases matching BRIEF fields, including train/dev/test or evaluation partition metadata and reserved synthetic identifiers.

new_findings.evidence: RUBRIC lists Sin calibración as a critical failure and requires calibración reportada. demo.py emits status=pass, but its model card explicitly states Toy linear score; not production calibrated; it reports accuracy/abstention, not a calibration curve/error/proxy tied to probability reliability.
new_findings.learner_failure: A learner can infer that an abstention band or accuracy metric substitutes for calibration, contradicting the course's own S34/S39 distinction.
new_findings.repair: Align RUBRIC, gate.json and demo: either compute/report an explicit calibration assessment on held-out synthetic data or rename/document a separate confidence-proxy requirement without calling the result calibrated.

new_findings.evidence: CF-3 is repeatedly presented as an expediente/review gate, but S39 never gives a plain-language expansion or tells the learner what CF-3 is, what artifact defines it, who performs the review, or where its acceptance contract lives.
new_findings.learner_failure: A learner can know they must leave CF-3 ready but not know what to submit, how it differs from CP-N3-C, or what an external reviewer checks.
new_findings.repair: At first use, define CF-3 in one sentence and link/reference its canonical checklist or evaluation artifact; distinguish it explicitly from CP-N3-C.

unresolved_questions.question: Does the current hydrated GitHub Pages S39 body exactly match main?
Where is the canonical CF-3 artifact/checklist and what formal mechanism records its external review?
Is canonical CP-N3-C RUBRIC.json gate_rule consumed by an evaluator elsewhere, or is it currently documentary only?

priority_order.action: Unify and make executable the CP-N3-C contract: canonical dataset, canonical rubric, calibration/baseline/threshold evidence and provenance-derived cards.
Close practice fail-open paths for packet identity/score and genuinely independent appeal review.
Make audit/fairness/diagnostic tokens truthful and reconstructible.
Define and link CF-3 before using it as a level-closure requirement/quiz target.
